approach.method_basis: The Parent generates fresh molecular graph neighbors and learns only from the current session's accepted scores. It fits a fixed boosted-tree regressor to ordered pairs of molecular count vectors and their score differences. For each new candidate it averages every accepted reference score plus its predicted difference, then adds the original count-GP correlated residual. The GP's original mean still controls stalled-pool eligibility. Accepted scores update the complete archive, top survivors and subsequent breeding.
approach.novelty: Replace the active pair learner with one scalar score function trained once on each real accepted molecule and score. Every predicted difference then comes from subtracting two values of that same function, enforcing self equality, opposite directions and closed cycles. This changes the learned function class: the Parent's all-reference averaging and the earlier reciprocity trial kept the unconstrained pair learner. The hypothesis is that enforcing one shared score improves prospective prediction and changes useful paid choices; exact consistency alone does not establish either benefit.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting Parent behavior is a structurally inconsistent active predictive location that remains less accurate than the retained GP on actual purchases. On n-ff10f4d5e7f3's complete Search panel, original logs and trajectories reproduce 435 fits/pools and 4350 prediction-to-label joins, all-reference MSE 0.008649387924947863 versus same-state GP 0.0054658416803000385, with raw pool self absolute mean 0.017277698110454324 and swap absolute mean 0.02472629956298779. Its all-reference mechanism is confirmed: versus its passive incumbent rule it changes 364 purchase sets and buys 784 actual-only identities, improves MSE from 0.00918329073879438, and its issued complete code-Parent paired macro delta is +0.022186684530005312 (10 favorable/5 adverse cells; all three seed macros positive), reaching mean 0.5470301211919261 and population seed SD 0.024079340089135263. This is useful inherited support, not evidence that global consistency is already enforced or causes better endpoints. The original n-7e9f57600099 raw-D-versus-GP prediction stays refuted; its older Anchor pairing remains false/empty/null because of the lock mismatch. n-93efcfa0f760's complete reciprocity MSE improves by 0.00007122557282760768 while its separate code-Parent endpoint delta is -0.0038813612303220113; finalized task_safe=false versus Parent task_safe=true are retained protocol facts. Those variants do not test a learned scalar potential. A scalar restriction could discard useful interactions and change effective regularization when dependent pair rows become real-label rows; no accuracy or score gain is assumed. Evidence is restricted to the frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 and five issued tasks. Independently hashed original per-seed summary.json/run.log and all task logs/trajectories, complete derived cell audits and exact prediction recomputation are indexed at policy/scratch/r0073-01-improve-L01/input-manifest.json, panel-audit.json and prediction-recompute.json; each audit-seed-N-task.json cites its original trajectory and log. Full source interpretations and conditions were read in policy/nodes/n-ff10f4d5e7f3.json, policy/nodes/n-93efcfa0f760.json, policy/nodes/n-7e9f57600099.json and policy/nodes/n-cf8d309c06de.json. The formal Anchor remains mean 0.607030316211131 with literal target 0.609030316211131 and cannot be attained by this different-code-Parent ticket.

method_change.previous_method: Code Parent n-ff10f4d5e7f3: fresh fixed XGBoost on concatenated ordered count-vector pairs and raw score differences; uniform raw-direction all-accepted-reference location plus original GP residual/gate.
method_change.proposed_method: Fresh fixed XGBoost scalar g on each real accepted original count vector/raw label once; hard differences g(x)-g(i), collapsed uniform-reference calibration intercept, original GP residual/gate and one passive unchanged raw pair comparator.
method_change.rationale: The actual code Parent has complete execution and a supported all-reference gain, but its raw predictive location remains inconsistent and less accurate than its GP. Restricting differences to one scalar potential changes the component hypothesis class and necessarily changes its supervision/input width. This one joint component replacement does not isolate those necessary parts or claim that self/swap/cycle defects were proved to mediate the Parent error.

hypothesis: Hard scalar-potential predictive location inside m-000000000005. At each inherited pre-announcement accepted cutoff, fit a fresh scalar XGBoost g(c) on exactly one original 2048-count vector and raw score per real accepted identity, in accepted-serial order, with the inherited estimator, full settings, session-derived seed, float32 inputs/labels and missing=NaN convention. Promote each native scalar output to float64 before arithmetic. Define D_g(i,x)=g(c_x)-g(c_i), r_i=y_i-g(c_i), b=(serial float64 sum_i r_i)/n, and mu_g(x)=g(c_x)+b. This is the collapsed uniform all-accepted reference mean. Replace only the active location with mu_g; keep the original GP residual tensor, original-GP-mean eligibility and sequential sampled maxima. The shared potential removes arbitrary pair-specific self/swap/cycle inconsistency and may improve prospective raw-score prediction; b changes calibration only. One unchanged separately fitted raw pair learner remains passive on exactly the same accepted state solely for the frozen comparison. This is a component model-class replacement, not projection of the Parent pair matrix or a second adaptive trial.

finding_summary.headline: Hard consistency held, but prediction error rose despite a higher mean endpoint
finding_summary.insights: The borrowed gradient-potential identity operated exactly, and the fixed scalar additive-tree learner also operated. Their current-session molecular adaptation removed structural inconsistency but did not improve prospective accuracy: the error claim is refuted for this joint model, input and supervision replacement. This is distinct from a technical failure, insufficient evidence or absence of score improvement. The endpoint gain cannot be credited separately to consistency, fewer training rows or input width, and it does not establish that prediction improvement mediated the gain. The common reference intercept changes calibration only; it supplied no extra within-pool ranking information. On unequal real-score pairs within actual purchase batches, scalar ordering accuracy was 0.629921, raw accuracy 0.648888, and GP accuracy 0.692870, counting prediction ties half. This identifies a remaining predictive/ranking limitation that a different surrogate or ranking model could address; enforcing exact pair consistency alone did not remove it. The chemistry also rules out universal scaffold collapse: typed/generic scaffold counts increased to 2,021/1,330 from 1,969/1,240, and within-batch count-Tanimoto after excluding tiny fragments fell to 0.722287 from 0.749127. Yet related local families persist; 440 purchases still have at least 50 heavy atoms and 16 have at most 6, versus 607 and 8. Unusual heteroatom-halogen environments and absent explicit stereochemical/charge alternatives remain. A proposal operator or search scheme that creates coherent core/linker and functional-group alternatives could address that separate coverage limitation; the current evidence does not prove such a change would improve scores. The registered prospective intervention is settled on this panel, while the broader potential-model approach and the causal source of the endpoint gain remain open.
finding_summary.results: All 435 scalar fits ran correctly. Shared-potential self, swap and cycle checks passed, and the collapsed reference mean matched its explicit reconstruction. The scalar rule changed 425 of 435 purchased sets and produced 1,521 purchases outside the passive raw rule's selected sets; 1,469 of those had strict same-availability choice changes. Nevertheless, over all 4,350 actual purchases, scalar mean squared error was 0.0140449655462, versus 0.0120512344903 for the unchanged raw all-reference predictor and 0.00792656273254 for the original GP. The strict preregistered prediction therefore failed. All 2,175 late purchases, 4,200 next-fit joins and 150 terminal censors are retained; there was no technical failure or missing essential comparator evidence. The independent endpoint result was favorable in aggregate: mean score 0.57080354777 versus 0.547030121192, a gain of 0.0237734265776, exceeding the conditional 0.002 target. Nine of 15 cells improved and six worsened; seed differences were +0.0851969921841, +0.00890424816422 and −0.0227809606154. This ticket uses a different code Parent than the formal-Anchor criterion requires, so that criterion is not attained.

molecular.headline: Smaller, varied ring systems still carry halogenated heteroatoms and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Source node n-a53bc2587706, code Parent n-ff10f4d5e7f3, profile epoch 1, batch ten, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, all fifteen paired task cells; 4,350 accepted optimizer purchases per node, excluding the 150 supplied initial records. All thirty original trajectories were read, each with 300 accepted rows: ten supplied initials and 290 optimizer purchases. The Child is rich in rings and aromatic atoms: median four perceived rings and fourteen aromatic atoms, with aromatic atoms in 4,095 of 4,350 purchases. Aromatic amides, linked heteroaromatics, carbonyl-rich N-rings and amine-bearing ring/linker systems recur, alongside compact nonaromatic fluorinated ring families. Median size is 32 heavy atoms versus 33 for the Parent; the full ranges are 2–120 and 1–120. The Child has 14 purchases at <=5 heavy atoms, 16 at <=6, 440 at >=50 and 431 at >50; the corresponding Parent counts are 8, 8, 607 and 597. This reduces the aggregate large tail while preserving both extremes and different behavior across tasks. There are 2,021 typed and 1,330 generic Murcko scaffolds, versus 1,969 and 1,240; empty acyclic scaffolds are included. Pair-count-weighted count-Tanimoto within task/seed cells is 0.616405 versus 0.652628, or 0.620654 versus 0.654981 after excluding <=6-heavy-atom fragments. Within ten-purchase batches it is 0.717533 versus 0.746456, or 0.722287 versus 0.749127 with those fragments excluded. The modestly broader global coverage is not explained solely by tiny fragments, but local series remain related and the change is not uniform across tasks. The fingerprint is radius-2, chirality-aware, 2048-bin Morgan counts with generalized dot-product Tanimoto; no cross-session pairs are compared. There are 443 N–halogen-bearing, 181 O–halogen-bearing, 170 S–halogen-bearing and 111 O–O-bearing purchases, versus 760, 125, 110 and 59. Carbon-centred two-double-bond flags occur in 160 purchases, of which 159 have cyclic instances; sulfur-centred two-double-bond flags occur in 182 and are recorded separately. The synthetic-plausibility reading is questionable because these unusual environments, repeated large assemblies and complex fused rings coexist with conventional medicinal-chemistry motifs. This is structural review, not measured stability, synthesis, pKa, toxicity or biological activity. No formal charge, assigned tetrahedral centre or specified double-bond stereochemistry occurs; 2,723 purchases carry 6,890 unassigned tetrahedral centres, versus 2,672 and 6,666 for the Parent. Explicit charge absence does not mean that neutral amines cannot ionize. The trusted complete matched code-Parent comparison has Child mean 0.5708035477695717, Parent mean 0.5470301211919261 and delta +0.023773426577645657. All six adverse endpoint cells remain in the task readings; the seed macro deltas are +0.08519699218406707, +0.008904248164220974 and -0.022780960615351065. Those are finite-panel score associations with complete Parent pairing, no missing trajectories or profile-mismatched seeds. They do not attribute a chemical change to an individual replaced component, establish transferable benefit, or satisfy the separate formal-Anchor criterion. Top/bottom-87 subsets use recorded optimizer scores with seed/evaluation tie-breaking; they are descriptive subsets, not independent replications. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
